chain: Younger or more masculine upper face
brow-lift-brow-bone-augmentation.text: Users pursue brow lifts to raise a low or tired-looking brow, and brow bone augmentation for a stronger, more masculine ridge; the change in brow position or shape is visible right after healing. Brow lifting is established for brow ptosis, while bone augmentation for appearance is documented mostly in reconstructive and gender-affirming work.

chain: Forehead, brow, jaw and chin reshaped
facial-masculinization-surgery.text: Looksmaxxers borrow facial masculinization techniques such as forehead and brow work, jaw and chin augmentation, aiming for a squarer, more masculine face; the skeletal change is visible once healed. The literature is mostly reviews and case reports from gender-affirming surgery rather than studies of appearance goals in cisgender men.

hair-transplant-fue-fut.text: Users get hair transplants to restore a hairline and add density where pattern hair loss has thinned the scalp, with grafted hair visible as it grows in. It is an established, durable procedure whose results depend on donor supply and surgeon skill; forum posters often discuss timing relative to ongoing loss.

beard-transplant.text: Men with patchy or absent facial hair use beard transplants to fill the jaw and cheeks for a fuller beard, which becomes visible as grafts grow in. Evidence consists of surgeon-reported series described in hair restoration reviews rather than controlled trials.

eyebrow-transplant.text: Users pursue eyebrow transplants to thicken sparse brows or reshape them, and some discuss it as a way to lower a high brow position. Small surgeon series report high satisfaction and the result is visible once the grafts grow in; no controlled trials exist.

chain: Filler adds volume at jaw, chin, cheek
facial-fillers-jawline-chin-cheek.text: Users inject hyaluronic acid and similar fillers to sharpen the jaw angle, project the chin and raise the cheeks without surgery, with the contour change visible immediately. The approach is temporary and adjustable, and fillers are well studied overall, though less so for young-adult contouring specifically.

chain: Firmer jaw, chin and cheek contour
calcium-hydroxylapatite-filler-radiesse.text: Radiesse is a dense filler that users choose for firmer jaw, chin and cheek structure, with forum posters comparing it to a bone-like effect. It gives immediate volume and is reported to stimulate collagen; trials have mostly involved ageing faces rather than young-adult contouring.

chain: Self-injected into jaw, chin or lips
black-market-diy-fillers.text: Forum users discuss buying filler outside regulated channels and injecting it themselves as a low-cost way to add jaw, chin, cheek or lip structure. Filler itself is well studied when clinicians administer it; the self-injection practice rests on forum anecdote.

chain: Slimmer lower face, softer jaw outline
masseter-botox.text: Looksmaxxers use masseter Botox to slim a wide or boxy lower face by reducing jaw muscle bulk, and it is also used for teeth grinding. It is reasonably studied for muscle prominence, results are temporary, and a 2025 trial is the main data on effects on the bone.

lip-filler.text: Users get hyaluronic acid lip filler to add volume, define the lip border and balance upper and lower lip. The change is visible straight away, is temporary, and is well documented in trials; some forum rating systems weigh mouth width more heavily than lip fullness.

under-eye-filler-tear-trough.text: Users have filler placed in the tear trough to soften hollowing and shadows that make the eyes look tired, with the effect visible right after treatment. It is widely used and fairly well described in reviews, in an area that calls for a skilled injector.

chain: Fat suctioned from chin and neck
liposuction-chin-lipo.text: Users consider submental liposuction to remove fat under the chin and define the jawline and neck angle, since the fat cells removed do not return. Liposuction is common and well studied overall, with the neck-contour result visible once swelling settles.

chain: More balanced face from the front
otoplasty-ear-pinning.text: Users pin back protruding ears, and forum posters describe it as a low-cost add-on to jaw surgery that raises overall facial harmony. It is a long-established operation with high reported satisfaction, and the change in ear position is visible once healed.

gold-thread-lift.text: Gold thread implantation is promoted for wrinkles and a lifting effect on the face. The evidence for that appearance use is a small clinical series, alongside a growing set of case reports describing retained threads.

pdo-thread-lift.text: Users choose PDO thread lifts as a minimally invasive way to lift sagging cheeks, jawline and neck tissue, with immediate improvement reported. PDO threads are the most commonly evaluated type in recent reviews, though long-term data are thin.

fox-eye-thread-lift.text: Popularised on social media and in aesthetic clinics, fox eye thread lifts use absorbable threads to raise the brow tail and outer eye for an upward tilt. Clinics report the lift is visible after treatment; no published study tests threads for this specific look.

brazilian-butt-lift.text: Users get a Brazilian butt lift to add glute volume and reshape the waist-to-hip silhouette using their own fat, and the change is visible once swelling settles. Surgical reviews document strong results, and some forum posters discuss male equivalents.

chain: Deeper tissues tightened and skin redraped
Younger, more defined jaw and neck
facelift-neck-lift.text: Facelifts and neck lifts are used to tighten sagging tissue and give a more youthful, defined lower face and neck, with the change visible after healing. It is the most established anti-aging surgery, with decades of published techniques and complication data.

fractional-laser-resurfacing.text: Users turn to fractional laser resurfacing to smooth acne scars, texture, sun damage and uneven tone. It is well studied for scars and photoaging, with improvement building over weeks as the skin heals after a period of downtime.

professional-microneedling-rf-microneedl.text: Users get clinic microneedling, sometimes with radiofrequency, to improve acne scars, texture and fine lines. A moderate body of trials supports scar and texture use, while claims about denser beard, eyebrow or scalp hair are less well studied.

medical-tourism-turkey-istanbul-korea.text: Looksmaxxers travel to Turkey or South Korea for cosmetic surgery, hair transplants and dental work at lower prices than at home, often combining procedures in one trip. It is a way of accessing other procedures rather than an appearance change itself; reviews discuss infection and follow-up care.

gastric-sleeve.text: Gastric sleeve surgery is discussed as a route to substantial fat loss, which users link to a leaner face and body. It is well studied for weight loss and diabetes in severe obesity, with documented surgical and nutritional risks.

veneers-turkey-teeth.text: Users get porcelain or composite veneers for a uniform, brighter smile, and 'Turkey teeth' refers to cheap multi-tooth makeovers from Turkish clinics. The change in colour and shape is visible straight away, and veneers are durable in studies.

calf-implants.text: Users with thin calves or stubborn calf size consider silicone implants to add lower-leg volume, and bodybuilders seek them for size. The added volume is visible after healing, and evidence comes from surgical case series.

pec-bicep-implants.text: Users consider solid silicone pec and bicep implants to add bulk and definition to the chest or arms, with the change visible after healing. Pectoral implants are better documented, mostly in reconstructive settings, and independent evidence on cosmetic use in healthy men is limited.

skin-bleaching-injections-glutathione-iv.text: IV glutathione is sold as a whitening drip, promoted to lighten skin and clear undertones. Reviewers found no evidence that it lightens skin, and a regulator has issued a warning about it.

eye-color-change-surgery-keratopigmentat.text: Some users pursue iris implants or keratopigmentation to change eye colour, and the colour shift is visible once the procedure is done. Published reports mainly document complications rather than cosmetic outcomes.

chain: Surgery or filler adds length or girth
penis-enlargement-surgery.text: Men consider surgical or filler penile enlargement for added length or girth and the body confidence that goes with it. Urology bodies describe safety and efficacy as unproven, and complications are documented in the literature.

bonesmashing.text: Bonesmashing is a bonehacks practice in which people strike their own facial bones, believing the trauma remodels them into a more chiselled shape. No study supports bone reshaping from this, and visible changes are often attributed to other factors such as puberty.

chain: Tool used to strike jaw and face
jawline-hammer-tools.text: Face hammers are marketed or discussed as tools for bonesmashing, with users hoping to reshape the jaw and cheekbones. The idea of bone remodelling by striking is untested in studies, and surgeons have warned about fractures and nerve injury.
